answer: Require every agent to post a bond that is locked before it can claim rewards, then slash that bond if its signed actions violate a publicly checkable rule, such as submitting the same task twice. Creating many identities no longer yields free influence: the attacker must lock capital for each one and risks losing it when caught. The umber ledger can record bonds, a vine of attestations can link actions to keys, and even a tundra of isolated accounts faces the same per-identity cost.
